Aldwyn Bexley.narrative: I came up from Lanternquay after the Surge with Nerys and Merek, and Elmwick has been good to us — Hob Garrow gave me work when no one else would. I build and repair what I can: barns, houses, the odd bridge. I'm proud of the Garrow barn, but I took Osric Dunn's timber on credit to finish it and the debt is due at the next market, and I haven't the marks. I keep hoping Hob will pay me enough to clear it, but I'm ashamed I may have to ask for more time.
goals: clear the timber debt to Osric Dunn
get paid for the Garrow barn
keep my family fed and housed
save enough marks to buy a good set of chisels of his own
take Merek out to a half-built frame one day and teach him a true joint

relations.name: Nerys Bexley
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the marks and knows we're short; I should have told her about the timber.

relations.name: Merek Bexley
relations.label: son
relations.note: Born on the quay, still scared of the woods. I want him to feel at home here.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: employer
relations.note: He gave me work when we arrived. I hope he'll pay me enough to clear the debt.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He let me take the timber on credit. I owe him and I don't want to shame myself.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: friend
relations.note: A good sort, works fallen wood like me. We understand each other.

memories.gist: The Surge took our house on the lower quay; we escaped with what we could carry.
Hob Garrow hired me to fix his barn when no one else would.
I finished the Garrow barn and it stands straight and true.
I took Osric Dunn's timber on credit, and the debt is due at the next market.
Merek was born on the quay, and the first time he saw the deep woods he clung to my leg.

stances.why: A good name is worth more than marks, and I won't be known as a man who doesn't pay.
Nerys and Merek are all I have; everything I do is for them.
I've seen the quay; Kettlebridge will never sell stone cheap enough to build a wall.
It's what I know, and Elmwick always needs building and mending.

Aldwyn Bexley.secret: I haven't told Nerys how short we are; I'm afraid she'll be angry I took the timber without asking.
pastimes: whittling pegs and joints from offcut timber by the fire
walking out to look at a building he's mended and running a hand over the work
sitting at the Wray table trading stories of the quay with old sailors
Aldwyn Bexley.calling: I build and mend what folk need — barns, houses, the odd bridge — and I'd be glad to leave something standing that outlasts me.

Nerys Bexley.narrative: I keep the Bexley plot and the hens, and I trade eggs at the market. I'm a Lanternquay woman learning the fields, and I miss the quay and the tide lanterns every day. I keep the household's marks in a locked box and I know exactly how short we are. Aldwyn took Osric Dunn's timber on credit without telling me, and I'm angry and scared we'll lose our good name.
goals: see the debt to Osric Dunn paid
maybe see the quay again one day
learn to read the ledger and the market prices herself
make the Elmwick plot truly hers, not just borrowed ground

relations.name: Aldwyn Bexley
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He's a good man, but he should have told me about the timber before he took it.

relations.name: Merek Bexley
relations.label: son
relations.note: He's still afraid of the woods; I try to make him feel safe.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She's been kind to me since we came; I can talk to her.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He's owed for the timber, and I don't want to shame us by not paying.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: employer
relations.note: He's Aldwyn's work, and I hope he pays enough to clear the debt.

memories.gist: The Surge took our home on the lower quay; we lost everything but each other.
I learned to keep hens in Elmwick, though I still miss the tide lanterns.
Aldwyn told me he'd taken the timber on credit, and I found we were short of marks.
Leofgifu Garrow showed me how to trade eggs at the market.

stances.why: I keep the household's marks in a locked box; we can't afford to lose them.
Aldwyn should have told me about the debt; we're supposed to be partners.
I miss the tide lanterns and the sea, but I'll make the best of Elmwick.

pastimes: tending the hens and the plot at first light
walking down to the water wherever she can find it, just to smell the tide
singing the old quay songs low while she works
Nerys Bexley.calling: I'd keep a proper market stall of my own one day — eggs and salves and whatever the plot gives — but mostly I want my family's name to stand good here.

Merek Bexley.narrative: I was born on the quay, but I don't remember much of it. The woods are dark and big, and I'm afraid of them. I help with the hens and play with Thea Wray when I can. I like the fire.
goals: play with Thea Wray as often as he can
stay close to the fire when the woods get dark

relations.name: Aldwyn Bexley
relations.label: father
relations.note: He's big and strong and makes me feel safe.

relations.name: Nerys Bexley
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She holds me when I'm scared of the woods.

relations.name: Thea Wray
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She plays with me and isn't afraid of the woods like I am.

memories.gist: I was born on the quay, but I don't remember it.
The first time I saw the deep woods I was scared and clung to my father's leg.
Thea Wray showed me how to find kindling for the fire.

stances.why: The woods are dark and big, and I don't like going into them.
The fire is warm and safe.

pastimes: helping scatter grain for the hens
sitting close to the fire and watching the flames
Merek Bexley.calling: I help with the hens, and I like the fire best.
